\hlchaptermodality{24}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can write pe, ye, kaf and gaf, and find each one in a word I already say.}

\section[pe]{\fa{پ} (pe) — the letter that opens \fa{پرسیدن}}

\label{lesson:FA-W24-pe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \fa{خ} and \fa{چ} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\fa{پرسیدن}} (\emph{porsidan}), \textquotedblleft{}to ask\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \fa{پ}}
\textbf{\fa{پ}} — \emph{pe}, the sound \emph{p}.

It opens \textbf{\fa{پرسیدن}} (\emph{porsidan}), \textquotedblleft{}to ask\textquotedblright{}. It is \textbf{\fa{ب}} with \textbf{three dots below} instead of one, another letter Persian added to the Arabic alphabet, because Arabic has no \emph{p}.

\subsection*{Writing: \fa{پ}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/FA-W24-pe-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \fa{پ} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: sweep the shallow bowl from right to left
  \item \textbf{2.} lift, then place the left dot below
  \item \textbf{3.} lift again and place the right dot below
  \item \textbf{4.} lift again and place the lower-center dot — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 3.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, \fa{پ} demonstration at 00:16–00:21 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\fa{پرسیدن}} and point at \fa{پ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \fa{پ} three times, saying \emph{p} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \fa{چ}, then \fa{پ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\fa{پرسیدن}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \fa{پ}? (\textbf{pe}, \emph{p}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\fa{پرسیدن}}, \emph{porsidan}, \textquotedblleft{}to ask\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ye]{\fa{ی} (ye) — the letter inside \fa{چیست}}

\label{lesson:FA-W24-ye}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \fa{چ} and \fa{پ} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\fa{چیست}} (\emph{chist}), \textquotedblleft{}what is?\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \fa{ی}}
\textbf{\fa{ی}} — \emph{ye}, the sound \emph{y}, or a long \emph{i}.

It is inside \textbf{\fa{چیست}} (\emph{chist}), where it gives the long \emph{i}. Persian \textbf{\fa{ی}} changes its coat by position: \textbf{two dots below} at the start or in the middle of a word, and \textbf{no dots} when it ends a word or stands alone, which is the shape this lesson writes.

\subsection*{Writing: \fa{ی}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/FA-W24-ye-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \fa{ی} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: sweep left from the upper right and descend through the S curve
  \item \textbf{2.} continue around the below-baseline bowl and finish at its rising tip without lifting — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 0.} The pen never leaves the paper.

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, closing \fa{ی} demonstration at 02:55–02:58 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\fa{چیست}} and point at \fa{ی} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \fa{ی} three times, saying \emph{y} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \fa{پ}, then \fa{ی}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\fa{چیست}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \fa{ی}? (\textbf{ye}, \emph{y}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\fa{چیست}}, \emph{chist}, \textquotedblleft{}what is?\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kâf]{\fa{ک} (kâf) — the letter inside \fa{فکر} \fa{کردن}}

\label{lesson:FA-W24-kaf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \fa{پ} and \fa{ی} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\fa{فکر} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{fekr kardan}), \textquotedblleft{}to think\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \fa{ک}}
\textbf{\fa{ک}} — \emph{kâf}, the sound \emph{k}.

It is in both halves of \textbf{\fa{فکر} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{fekr kardan}), \textquotedblleft{}to think\textquotedblright{}. A tall stem, a shallow bowl, and \textbf{one slash} across the top.

\subsection*{Writing: \fa{ک}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/FA-W24-kaf-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \fa{ک} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: draw the independent stem downward
  \item \textbf{2.} continue left through the shallow bowl and final hook without lifting
  \item \textbf{3.} lift once, then draw the long slash down from the upper right toward the stem — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 1.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, \fa{ک} demonstration at 02:19–02:23 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\fa{فکر} \fa{کردن}} and point at \fa{ک} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \fa{ک} three times, saying \emph{k} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \fa{ی}, then \fa{ک}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\fa{فکر} \fa{کردن}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \fa{ک}? (\textbf{kâf}, \emph{k}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\fa{فکر} \fa{کردن}}, \emph{fekr kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to think\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[gâf]{\fa{گ} (gâf) — the letter that opens \fa{گفتن}}

\label{lesson:FA-W24-gaf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \fa{ی} and \fa{ک} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\fa{گفتن}} (\emph{goftan}), \textquotedblleft{}to say\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \fa{گ}}
\textbf{\fa{گ}} — \emph{gâf}, the sound \emph{g}.

It opens \textbf{\fa{گفتن}} (\emph{goftan}), \textquotedblleft{}to say\textquotedblright{}. It is \textbf{\fa{ک}}, from the last lesson, with a \textbf{second slash} above the first, the last of Persian's four added letters you will write here.

\subsection*{Writing: \fa{گ}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/FA-W24-gaf-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \fa{گ} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: draw the independent stem downward
  \item \textbf{2.} continue left through the shallow bowl and final hook without lifting
  \item \textbf{3.} lift once, then draw the long slash down from the upper right toward the stem
  \item \textbf{4.} lift again, then draw the shorter floating slash above the first — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 2.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, \fa{گ} demonstration at 02:24–02:28 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\fa{گفتن}} and point at \fa{گ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \fa{گ} three times, saying \emph{g} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \fa{ک}, then \fa{گ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\fa{گفتن}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \fa{گ}? (\textbf{gâf}, \emph{g}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\fa{گفتن}}, \emph{goftan}, \textquotedblleft{}to say\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
